curriculum_expectations.E2.1: use appropriate units of length to estimate, measure, and compare the perimeters of polygons and curved shapes, and construct polygons with a given perimeter
curriculum_expectations.E2.2: explain the relationships between millimetres, centimetres, metres, and kilometres as metric units of length, and use benchmarks for these units to estimate lengths
curriculum_expectations.E2.3: use non-standard units appropriately to estimate, measure, and compare capacity, and explain the effect that overfilling or underfilling, and gaps between units, have on accuracy
curriculum_expectations.E2.4: compare, estimate, and measure the mass of various objects, using a pan balance and non-standard units
curriculum_expectations.E2.5: use various units of different sizes to measure the same attribute of a given item, and demonstrate that even though using different-sized units produces a different count, the size of the attribute remains the same
curriculum_expectations.E2.6: use analog and digital clocks and timers to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds
curriculum_expectations.E2.7: compare the areas of two-dimensional shapes by matching, covering, or decomposing and recomposing the shapes, and demonstrate that different shapes can have the same area
curriculum_expectations.E2.8: use appropriate non-standard units to measure area, and explain the effect that gaps and overlaps have on accuracy
curriculum_expectations.E2.9: use square centimetres (cm2) and square metres (m2) to estimate, measure, and compare the areas of various two-dimensional shapes, including those with curved sides
